courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Brain & Behavior I
courses.description: Graduate standing required. A survey of psychological and biological approaches to the study of sensory and perceptual information processing, with an emphasis on touch and pain.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Brain & Behavior II
courses.description: A survey of psychological and biological approaches to the study of basic learning and higher integrative processing.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Advanced Biological Psychology: Central Nervous System
courses.description: Each fall one special topic will be covered in depth (e.g., neural bases of memory storage, homeostasis, and perception). Format includes lectures and seminar meetings with student presentations.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Applications of Experimental Psychology to Health Research
courses.description: This course provides a critical analysis of interdisciplinary research within experimental psychology, including such topics as psychopharmacology, psychoneuroimmunology, psychophysiology, and animal models of brain/behavior disorders.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
courses.description: Basic principles of pharmacology and behavior analysis are considered in relation to drugs that affect the central nervous system.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PSYC 404; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: NBIO 705. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PSYC 404 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | PSYC 705 , PHCO 705 .

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Research Design and Statistics in Neuroscience
courses.description: Limited to graduate students in psychology, neuroscience, and neurobiology. Experimental design, hypothesis testing, power analyses, ANOVAs, regression, correlations. Hands on data analysis with you being able to use your own data sets. Analyses will be conducted with SPSS and Prism. Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Advanced Light Microscopy
courses.description: An intensive and comprehensive hands-on laboratory-oriented course in light microscopy for researchers in biology, medicine, and materials science. This course will focus on advanced quantitative fluorescence microscopy techniques used for imaging a range of biological specimens, from whole organisms, to tissues, to cells, and to single molecules. This course emphasizes the quantitative issues that are critical to the proper interpretation of images obtained with light microscopes.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Introductory Pain Neurobiology
courses.description: Advanced level understanding of the underlying biological processes that contribute to the transmission and modulation of acute and chronic pain and pharmacologic management of acute and chronic pain: detailing the mechanism of action of commonly used drugs as well as exploring new drug targets.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology
courses.description: Introduces topics including brain cell biology, molecular biology applied to neurons, membrane potentials and imaging methods. The second block introduces such topics as resistance, capacitance, passive membranes, classes of ion channels, potassium and calcium channels, and action potential initiation. Final blocks, focus on neurotransmitter release and signaling through distinct receptor subclasses. Topics include G-protein coupled receptors and associated signaling, receptor binding/ligand theory, ionotropic and metabotropic glutamate and GABA receptors, receptor trafficking and localization. Permission of the department.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology: Introduction and Electrical Signaling
courses.description: Permission of the department. This course explores the experimental and theoretical function of the nervous system. Typically, the first hour is fundamental material presentation and the second hour may be a presentation led by the students. Topics covered include: cellular diversity in the CNS, gross brain anatomy, human and rodent brain imaging, neuromolecular genetics, behavioral methods, membrane potentials/resistance/capacitance, ion channel structure, electrophysiology and propagation of electrical signals in neurons. Basic undergraduate biology, chemistry, physics and intro calculus is assumed.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology: Postsynaptic Mechanisms-Receptors
courses.description: Permission of the department. Consideration of membrane receptor molecules activated by neurotransmitters in the nervous system with emphasis on ligand binding behavior and molecular and functional properties of different classes of receptors. Course meets for four weeks with six lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology
courses.description: Block one covers neural stem cells, glial development, neural cell death and neurotrophin. The second block introduces the sensory pathways of vision, audition, taste, olfaction, pain, and touch, and the motor pathways of the spinal cord, basal ganglia, cerebellum, and motor cortex. Includes sensory information processing, motor execution, peripheral and central mechanisms of pain. Final block covers CNS imaging, regeneration, and such diseases as Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's, epilepsy, addiction, autism, and schizophrenia. Permission of the department required.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Developmental Neurobiology
courses.description: A survey of nervous system development emphasizing detailed analysis of selected research topics such as neuronal induction, neural crest development, neuronal differentiation, synapse formation, neurotrophic factors, glial development, and the effects of experience.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, NBIO 722; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: NBIO 724. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisite, NBIO 722 ; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Experimental Neurophysiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Six or more laboratory hours a week.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Translational Seminar in Cognitive and Clinical Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduces new neuroimaging techniques and their application to the study of neural correlates of cognitive and behavioral impairments in brain disorders. Reviews the theories and research methodologies that investigate how brain functions support and give rise to mental operations such as attention, memory, emotions, social cognition in the healthy brain.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Diseases of the Nervous System
courses.description: Explores the basic neurobiology and the clinical aspects of a range of diseases of the nervous system, including ALS, Alzheimer's, autism, schizophrenia, multiple sclerosis, deafness, epilepsy, pain, brain tumors, stroke, Parkinson's, and other neurodegenerative diseases.

source.text: NBIO 728. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisites, NBIO 201, or 722 and 223.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Sensory Neural Information Processing and Representation
courses.description: Additional required preparation, one year of calculus, familiarity with MATLAB or Python, or permission of the instructor. A discussion/reading seminar covering the fundamentals of nervous system information processing and integration, with examples from sensory systems.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Microscopy: Principles & Applications
courses.description: This course aims to provide the knowledge one may need to understand the reach of microscopy imaging techniques, to be able to choose the right imaging modality, label the sample, carry out the experiment, analyze data, troubleshoot any pitfalls that may occur, and put together a custom optical setup.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Biological Concepts
courses.description: Overview of structures and biological determinants of conditions and diseases of the oral cavity. Both growth and development and pathophysiology will be introduced in the context of three areas of oral biology: biology of extracellular matrices, host-pathogens interactions, and orofacial neurobiology.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Neurocircuits and Behavior Journal Club
courses.description: This is journal club course will meet once per week for 90 minutes to discuss new research papers focused on delineating how neurocircuits function to orchestrate various behavioral states. Papers for discussion will be chosen by the instructor and students, and students will rotate in leading discussions.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Seminar in Chemical Neurobiology
courses.description: Required preparation, two semesters of biochemistry.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Neuroanalytics: Introduction to Big Data Science for Neuroscientists
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide both practical and theoretical training in advanced data analysis approaches commonly used in neuroscience research. Making biological insights into complex neuroscience data requires familiarity with computer programming, distributed computing, visualization, and statistics. This course aims to provide an introduction to these analysis techniques to make the aspiring neuroscientist comfortable with data science.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Neurodevelopmental Basis of Brain Disorders
courses.description: The basic principles guiding in the formation and maintenance of human nervous system and how do distinct genetic/ epigenetic disruptions during development cause different types of human neurodevelopmental disorders. The intent of this course is to present latest advances in developmental neuroscience in the context of this theme. Topics covered IMII include neural patterning, neurogenesis, neural cell ate specification, neuronal migration, axon/dendritic growth and connectivity.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Gene-Brain-Behavior Interactions in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Perspectives on Disease Mechanisms
courses.description: This seminar examines the topics of genetics, neuroanatomy, physiology, and behavioral development to provide a broad-based and integrated background to understand the etiology and potential mechanism underlying neurodevelopmental disorders.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Clinical Syndromes and Neurodevelopmental Disorders
courses.description: This seminar will review the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis and treatment of neurodevelopmental syndromes and disorders. Topics will range from single gene (e.g. fragile X syndrome and tuberous sclerosis) to complex genetic (e.g., autism, schizophrenia), to environmental disorders with varied phenotypes, pathogenetic mechanisms, and treatments.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Improving Presentation & Communication of Scientific Results
courses.description: Learning modern day techniques and approaches to convey scientific results effectively as a public speaker. Teaching how to implement the key aspects of effective presentation of scientific findings in public settings. Understanding the key components of an effective public talk including scientific content, body language, and voice. Learning how to captivate the target audience and yet still convey data driven scientific findings.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Seminar in Comparative Animal Behavior
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced seminar in comparative animal behavior. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Seminar in Comparative Physiology
courses.description: Advanced seminar in comparative physiology.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Special Topics in Neurobiology
courses.description: Special topics in neurobiology. Content will vary from semester to semester.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Special Topics in Physiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Individually arranged in-depth programs of selected topics such as membrane function, transport physiology, renal physiology, etc.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Neuroscience Seminar Series
courses.description: Diverse but current topics in all aspects of neuroscience. Relates new techniques and current research of notables in the field of neuroscience. Content focuses on presentations by invited, non-UNC faculty, UNC faculty and mini-series presentations from current Neuroscience students. Topics vary from week to week.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Research in Neurobiology
courses.description: Permission of the department. Research in various aspects of neurobiology. Six to 24 hours a week.

courses.subject: NBIO
courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.description: Course is designed to certify that the students have achieved a high level of knowledge competence in clinical and basic neurosciences, without the rigorous research experience required of a Ph.D.
